text: Welcome to the Beginner AWS Capstone. Over these ten lessons you're going to take one real stakeholder question and answer it using the smallest real AWS stack that can do the job properly — no shortcuts, but also nothing you don't need. We're staying with Northfield Outdoor Supply, the camping and hiking gear retailer from the main capstone, but earlier in their story, before any of that bigger pipeline existed.

Here's where things stand. Someone on Northfield's IT team set up a single S3 bucket, northfield-raw-zone, and the Operations Manager pulled a month of order exports from the on-prem SQL Server and dropped them in, one CSV file per day, for all of August. Now that same Operations Manager wants an answer: which product category sold the most? I want to know what to restock first.

That question is answerable with a surprisingly small stack. Raw CSV files already sit in S3. A Glue Crawler reads those files and builds a table in the Glue Data Catalog, without copying or moving a single byte. And Athena runs real SQL directly against the files sitting in S3. Three services, no new storage system, no pipeline running on a schedule.

But first, the question itself needs sharpening. Which category sold the most could mean units moved or revenue earned, and those aren't always the same category — a cheap item can outsell an expensive one in volume while losing on revenue. Since the real goal is deciding what to restock, the real spec becomes: show total units sold and total revenue by product category, for August 2026, from the files already in northfield-raw-zone.

And just as important as what's in scope is what's deliberately left out. This project stays at S3, Glue Crawler, and Athena. It does not build a Glue ETL transformation job, and it does not load anything into Redshift. There's no recurring reporting workload here — just one ad-hoc question — so reaching for a data warehouse would be solving a problem Northfield doesn't actually have yet.

That's the business ask, turned into a real, specific requirement. Next lesson, we sketch the plan for this discovery pipeline in plain English — S3, Glue Crawler, Athena, and why that's exactly the right-sized stack for this job — before opening the AWS console at all.
